title: Why a Hat Maker Paid $225 for One Concert Ticket #history #shorts
description:
In September 1850, P. T. Barnum auctioned the first tickets to Jenny Lind's first concert in New York. The winning bid for the first ticket was $225, from John Genin, the hatter next door to Barnum's museum. The next ticket went for $25, and the New York Herald said Genin's seat was by no means the best one.

He wasn't paying for the seat. Every important newspaper in the country printed his name, and Barnum later wrote that the purchase laid the foundation of Genin's fortune. A year later, when the Hungarian leader Louis Kossuth arrived in New York, Genin gave his party hats from unsold stock for their parade up Broadway, then sold the rest.

What if you were in that crowd in 1850 with only your phone? Full video: https://youtu.be/xNUNnDS4BiY
